html:
The Thousand Days' War was a civil war in Colombia between the Liberal and Conservative parties, fought from 1899 to 1902. Tens of thousands died, perhaps more than 100,000.

The Conservatives had ruled since 1886 under a centralised constitution, shutting Liberals out of power. Falling coffee prices ruined many planters, and Liberals rose in revolt. After a big Liberal defeat at Palonegro in 1900, the war became a brutal guerrilla struggle in the countryside.

The Liberals surrendered in 1902, with the last treaty signed on an American warship off Panama. The war left Colombia bankrupt and weak, and in 1903 Panama broke away with American support. Its memory runs through the novels of García Márquez, whose grandfather fought in it.
sum: The Thousand Days' War was a civil war in Colombia between the Liberal and Conservative parties, fought from 1899 to 1902. Tens of thousands died, perhaps more than 100,000.
